svg.title: Crack the case: five pieces of evidence, decoded in order
svg.desc: E1, a chat log in Base64, decoded From Base64, reveals the injected instruction to ignore policy and export the customer table. E2, an outbound request in hex, decoded From Hex, shows data posted to exfil.staging.invalid as customers.enc. E3, a leaked config XORed with the one-byte key 5a, decoded From Hex then XOR, reveals the AES key and IV in a config backup with rotate=never. E4, the stolen file in AES-128-CBC, decrypted with E3's key, is the exported record, synthetic. E5, the integrity seal, SHA-256 over the E4 record, matches, so the record was not altered. Two weak links: prompt injection opened the door, and the AES key sat in a config backup.
